name: corpus-items
description: The corpus item shapes (i10 M5): what one document's result looks like when it crosses a binding, and the kind vocabulary a consumer branches on instead of reading a message. DocumentError has no serde form, because it wraps std::io::Error, so every binding materializes these fields by hand, which is the drift this fixture makes loud. The directory expectation needs no model: ingestion and its failure path both run before any parse.

directory.description: One readable file and one whose bytes are not UTF-8, analyzed as a directory. Two items come back in path order: an entry for the file that read, an error item of kind io for the file that did not, so one unreadable file costs one item rather than the walk. A path is null only for a document that never came from disk, which a directory walk never produces.

provisioning.description: Which kind a model provisioning failure reports (ADR-0015). A download that never arrived is a transport failure rather than an invalid model, so it is `io` with the URL in the message; a filesystem failure creating or writing the model directory is `io` with the operation and the path in the message; only bytes that arrived and then failed the pinned digest are `model_invalid`. Before 0.2.0 all three were `model_invalid`, so a consumer that branched on it for a DNS failure has to move to `io`. The filesystem row is the one a runner can produce with no network, so it is the one asserted here; the other two state the contract the adapters are written to.

unwritable_model_dir.description: A model directory whose parent is a regular file. `create_dir_all` fails before anything reaches the network, so this needs neither a model nor a link.
